Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and one small ask so we can prioritize next steps: 

- Current situation: BrightLayer is juggling slow inference on your in-house vector search pipeline and rising token costs when running cust-facing summarization. You mentioned 10–15% SLA misses during peak traffic and an interest in reducing per-token spend without losing response quality.
- Proposed pilot: Redwood Dedicated trial for 4 weeks, scope: inference for the document-summarization endpoint (up to 8k context) with a locked model profile, autoscaling to handle peak, and a simple eval set to monitor quality regressions.
- Expected outcomes: 30–40% reduction in per-token CPU/GPU cost via caching and batching, and predictable 99th percentile latency under 300ms for the pilot workload (our estimate based on the sample traces you shared).

Can you do me a quick favor? Is this still a priority for BrightLayer in the next 30–45 days, and who would be the final decision owner for a pilot (procurement/infra/engineering)? If you’re not the right person, feel free to point me to the best contact and I’ll loop them in.

I attached the one-page pilot MTP and my notes from today’s discovery ("20261115-brightlayer-mtp.pdf" and "discovery-notes-20261115.txt").

If it helps, here are two quick next steps we can take:
- Option A: Quick follow-up 20-min sync this week to align pilot scope and timeline (you can pick a slot here: https://calendar.redwoodinference.com/jordan/book?slot=30)
- Option B: I’ll send a short pilot statement of work and a rough cost estimate for your TPM to review offline.

No pressure — just want to make sure we’re aligned on priority before I pull engineering resources.

Best,

Jordan —

If you don’t get a response, a couple of low-friction plays we’ve used:
- Send one short email that asks for two choices (Yes → schedule 20m this week; No → not a priority; Maybe → send SOW). People pick one.
- Offer a technical office hour with an engineer (30m) to walk their TPM through the data/trace assumptions — less commitment than a formal pilot.
- If you have a VP or director-level exec contact, try a single-line note referencing the impact ("we estimate 30% reduction in X") — sometimes gets attention.

I can jump on the outreach if you want me to send the VP-level note.

—Ben
